tool_args.rationale: The pilot covers the target horizon, but it does not resolve the memory dynamics: every prefix follows a similar single-switch design, and each row supplies only one forecast endpoint. Acquire the finer trajectory batch to better separate memory relaxation from its coupling to the observed state before fitting and seeking fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the four-parameter coupled ODE now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Five endpoint labels at similar horizons leave little leverage to separate the memory time constant from coupling strength. The raw prefixes reconstruct the initial memory state for a given time constant but do not directly measure it.
Cheaper, but the pilot already points to history dependence. The main uncertainty is how fast the memory relaxes and how strongly it affects the forecast.

considered_alternatives.option: Single-mode Maxwell decay or Kelvin–Voigt creep
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Maxwell decay predicts opposite signs for upward and downward input steps, but all observed endpoints are positive. The stated Kelvin–Voigt law has no dependence on the initial state or its history.
